revisionDesc.change: Finalized - All corrections made by Zellmann-Rohrer have been taken up except that at the end of line 27. While τὼ seems better than τὸ, there is more going on there that has yet to be adequately explained. See voters' comments. In addition to these changes, inaccurate line numbering has been fixed and further clean-up has been performed.

Vote - AcceptText - I endorse what the previous voters have said and add the following:
The line numbers need to be corrected: ll. 28-29 in the DDBDP should be only l. 28, then l. 30 is actually l. 29, etc.
l. 27: agreed, the editor's α̣ὐ̣τ̣ὸ̣ is not convincing. The Michigan copies don't have anything similar in this position. At the end of P.Mich. V 323.29, after εἰς τὸ, there is a short horizontal that begins with a point. This could just be a filler stroke, but notice the short, horizontal stroke above πρόκειται at PSI VIII 903.28 (l. 29 in DDBDP). I think in both cases this is a paragraphos marking where the subscription should be written. In the PSI example, the writer let his subscription wander a full line above this mark, while in the Michigan example, the writer's first line comes up to meet this mark. I don't see this mark on 324 or 325. In this posiiton of the text in 324 and 325, moreover, there is no extra writing. Going back to the PSI text, there clearly is something written after τὼ. Perhaps τὼι̣ (dotted iota) is better, but even this doesn't get rid of all those strokes. The up and down curves at the end (before ἐπιβάλλων) look like how nu is written in ἐπιβάλλων. The one (?) letter before could be any number of things, if not the iota adscript. I would dot two letters and editorially cancel them from the text (not scribal deletion) on the strength of the parallels.

Vote - DEFER - ln 17: δουλήας is fine. Ln 19: λέλονχαν is good--add reg tag with regularized form? Ln. 26: συνκεχωρήκασιν, dot the rho? τριῶν ὁμο(λογούντων) is also good. Addressing Sosin's concern about this reading, I would adduce χοντα at the beginning of line 8 where the nu also shows an extra hump. It's unclear what's going on at the end of ln. 27 and for this reason I'm choosing to defer my vote. Both in the P.Mich. text (http://quod.lib.umich.edu/cgi/i/image/getimage-idx?cc=apis&entryid=X-1347&viewid=1264R.TIF&quality=large) and in this one there is more than εἰς τὸ (or τὼ) before ἐπιβάλλον. PSI 903 has〚α̣ὐ̣τ̣ὸ̣〛 (see p. XVII), but this isn't a totally convincing reading, and it doesn't square with the P.Mich. text. What does the next voter think?

Vote - AcceptText - Accept. Lin17 δουλήας is clear (as in P.Mich. 5.323.17 : http://quod.lib.umich.edu/cgi/i/image/getimage-idx?cc=apis&entryid=X-1347&viewid=1264R.TIF&quality=large ) ; lin19 in λέλονχαν the alpha is open as θαριον in lin14; and this is the reading P.Mich. 5.323.19; lin26 I think συνκεχωρήκασιν is right but I would underdot as follows: συνκεχω̣ρ̣ή̣κασιν ; lin26 end τριῶν is clear to me and so is ὁμο but I see a V shaped connector/letter between the two; that plus the omicron look exactly like το in χωριστου (χωρὶς τοῦ) directly above 2 lines (in 24); the new rdg is clearly superior to the ed pr and likely right, but I remain slightly worried by what looks to me like a surplus letter (τριωντομο) ; lin27 τὼ (l. τὸ) seems clear.

line 17: [δού]λης → δουλήας (l. δουλείας) based on digital image (psi-online): the word is visible in full, and confirmed by the reading of the duplicate, P.Mich. V 323.17 line 19: λελόνχασ̣ι̣ → λελόνχαν: nu seems clear, and the duplicate has the same spelling (line 19) line 19: entered BL correction lines 23-24: πεντα|κοσίας → φεντα|κοσίας (l. πεντακοσίας): the phi seems clear, and the same spelling appears in the duplicate (line 24) line 26: συνκεχωρηκ̣ό̣τ̣ε̣ς̣ → συνκεχωρήκασιν: alpha, sigma, iota, and nu seem clear, and this form appears also in the duplicate, line 27 line 26: τρι̣ῶ̣(ν) γε̣γρα̣μ(μένων) → τριῶν ὁμο(λογούντων): final nu of τριῶν seems clear; the second word is abbreviated, with omicron suprascript above the mu. Cf. the duplicate, 28: ὁμολογούντων τριῶν line 27: τὸ → τὼ (l. τὸ)
